speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you mentioned recurrent bronchitis, but I need to clarify: are you currently experiencing any fever, night sweats, or unintended weight loss alongside your chronic cough? These symptoms can help distinguish between chronic bronchitis and other conditions like tuberculosis or lung cancer.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given your history as a non-smoker with 11 years of productive cough and recurrent "bronchitis," have you ever noticed blue discoloration of your fingers or toes, or does your cough worsen specifically after being in a cold environment?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. Given your history of recurrent "bronchitis," chronic productive cough in a non-smoker, and the specific description of thick, purulent sputum, I am requesting a High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the chest to confirm the presence of dilated bronchi and rule out other etiologies.
